slides.texte_overlay:
Things every man
should own by 30
A good toolbox. Hammer, screwdrivers, a level, a drill. Hanging a shelf or fixing a loose door yourself saves money and gives you a quiet kind of confidence.
One great coat. Dark, well cut, the right size. A coat that fits makes every outfit underneath look sharper, all winter long, for many years to come.
A set of real kitchen knives. One chef's knife, one bread knife, one small knife. Cooking becomes faster, safer and far more enjoyable with proper tools.
A first aid kit you know how to use. Plasters, bandages, painkillers, a thermometer. Being ready when a friend gets hurt matters more than any gadget.
A shelf of books you've actually read. I add five minutes a day of history, art or science, and my mind gets the same care and attention I give my home.
slides.texte_sophia: A daily learning habit. I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. My mind gets the same care as my home.

slides.texte_overlay: A decent suit. Navy or charcoal, tailored to you. Weddings, interviews, funerals. Having one ready means you never panic when an important day comes up.
An emergency fund. Three months of basic costs set aside. It's not exciting, but it turns life's surprises into inconveniences instead of disasters.
